**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 1, 2026**
- **Member:** Morgan Alvarez
- **Member ID:** W375849485
- **Reference number:** POC-FB8E2AE06A-30252
- **Denied service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766), effective 07/01/2026 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, requested for me. The notice dated August 1, 2026 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking you to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file show that I completed conservative treatment and that it did not relieve my symptoms.

Below I have set out the plan's own criteria, quoted word for word from the guideline named above, next to what my records show.

---

### 1. The plan's conservative treatment requirement

The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;"

My records show more than the minimum this criterion describes. I completed supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over **8 weeks from May 15, 2026 to July 10, 2026, with 20 visits completed.** This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. Both the length of treatment and the timing fall within what the plan itself asks for.

### 2. The plan's requirement for the type of conservative treatment

The policy states:

> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

My treatment included both kinds of care, directed at my lumbar spine:

- **Active:** supervised physical therapy with core stabilization and lumbar flexibility exercises, 20 visits over 8 weeks.
- **Inactive:** NSAIDs taken for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026 that gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.

### 3. The plan's requirement that conservative care did not work

The policy lists, among the ways this can be shown:

> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR"

> "Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR"

My records show both a full course of treatment and a lack of meaningful improvement. I have had **24 months of progressive low back pain that is not relieved by rest.** The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief. The injection helped only partially, and only for about four weeks. After 20 physical therapy visits, I still **cannot stand for more than 10 minutes** and still have **radicular pain into my right calf.**

I want to be clear that I am not asking you to excuse me from treatment. The policy also allows for:

> "Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment"

and separately notes:

> "Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

Neither of those situations applies to me. I attended and completed my therapy. My appeal rests on the fact that the treatment was done and did not work.

### 4. The plan's requirement for radicular symptoms on exam

The policy states:

> "Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities"

My exam findings include **positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.** My symptoms clearly limit my daily activities: I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain running into my right calf.

### 5. The plan's imaging requirement

The policy states:

> "Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual’s symptoms/signs"

My **MRI of the lumbar spine dated May 29, 2026** shows an **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.** That finding is on the right side, at the level and nerve root that match my right-sided radicular leg pain and my exam findings.

### 6. The plan's documentation requirements

The policy states:

> "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery."

and:

> "All appropriate supporting documentation, including recent pertinent office visit notes, laboratory data, and results of any special testing must be provided."

The request in my file was submitted by Dr. Okafor, an orthopedic surgeon, for the procedure coded CPT 63030, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed for my condition. With this appeal I am submitting or asking Dr. Okafor's office to submit: my physical therapy discharge note covering May 15 – July 10, 2026; the May 29, 2026 lumbar MRI report; office visit notes documenting my exam findings and medication trial; the record of my May 14, 2026 corticosteroid injection; and Dr. Okafor's operative plan note dated [date of surgical plan note]. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I do not smoke.

The policy additionally asks for:

> "Documentation of an exercise prescription/plan provided by a physician, physical therapist, or chiropractor; AND"

> "Follow-up documentation regarding completion of HEP after the required 6-week timeframe or inability to complete HEP due to a documented medical reason (i.e., increased pain or inability to physically perform exercises)"

If the plan believes these specific documents are missing from what was submitted, I am asking that you identify them so my physical therapist and surgeon can supply them from my chart: [exercise prescription/home exercise program documentation and follow-up note, to be requested from the treating physical therapist]. My supervised therapy course itself is documented in the discharge note already in your file.

### 7. A point I am asking the plan to clarify

The guideline includes a provision that reads:

> "Microdiscectomy may be used as the first line of treatment (no conservative treatment required) in the following clinical scenarios:"

That sentence introduces a list of clinical scenarios that I do not have in front of me, so I am not making an argument based on those items. I am asking the plan to identify exactly which criteria it applied in denying my request, and which specific document it found lacking, so that I can respond to it directly. My appeal is based on the conservative-care pathway quoted above, which my records meet.

---

### What I am asking for

I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to reconsider and overturn the denial dated August 1, 2026, and to authorize the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by Dr. Okafor. The stated reason for the denial was an inadequate trial of conservative treatment. My records document eight weeks and 20 completed physical therapy visits from May 15 to July 10, 2026, along with four months of NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026, and they show continued pain and continued nerve-root compression on the May 29, 2026 MRI. I ask that these records be measured against the criteria quoted above in the plan's own words.

If you uphold this denial, I ask that you tell me in writing which criterion from the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766) my records did not meet, what specific documentation would satisfy it, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the decision. I also ask for a copy of the complete criteria used in my case and for information about my further appeal rights, including external review.

My appeal must be received by **January 28, 2027**, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I can also reach Member Services by phone at **1-888-333-4742**.

Please contact me if anything further would help, and please also share this appeal with Dr. Okafor's office so they can provide any additional records you need.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Alvarez**
